arguments.summary: Technical assessment as of the 2026-09-22 completed session: ANET has strong absolute momentum and 63-session leadership versus both SPY and XLK, but the path has been volatile. The only relative reversal is versus XLK: ANET lagged slightly over 5 sessions while leading over 21 and 63 sessions. Price is above rising short-, medium- and long-term averages and near the prior 21-session closing high, yet the latest volume was only near its prior median and the 63-session close-path drawdown reached 15.5060%. Historical regime-conditioned positive-return frequencies are lower than ANET's unconditional base rates at 5, 21 and 63 sessions; they are dependent overlapping analogs, not calibrated forecasts. The setup is therefore a conditional technical opportunity rather than evidence of low-risk persistence.

claims.text: On the 2026-09-22 completed session, ANET closed at $205.19. Split-adjusted price returns were +6.4043% over 5 sessions, +8.7676% over 21 and +26.5043% over 63. The close was 4.9533% above SMA20 ($195.506), 8.9237% above SMA50 ($188.3796) and 31.6234% above SMA200 ($155.89175). Annualized realized volatility was 22.4371%, 44.8032% and 55.0458% over the respective 5/21/63-session windows; the 252-session high drawdown was -2.5226%. These are completed-session observations, not intrinsic-value or forecast signals.

Matched-date, SIP-feed, split-adjusted price-return comparisons as of 2026-09-22: PAIR ANET/SPY 5=+4.2931 21=+7.7672 63=+21.0789
PAIR ANET/XLK 5=-0.4151 21=+1.6976 63=+19.9459
Thus ANET led SPY at every measured window, but against XLK it shifted from a slight 5-session lag to 21- and 63-session leadership. The data do not show a 63-session lag to either benchmark; the relevant tension is recent sector-relative softness despite longer-window leadership.

The technical path panel shows ANET's SMA20 rose 1.7405% over the latest five sessions, while the 2026-09-22 close remained 0.1120% below the prior 21-session closing high. Latest volume was 0.9790 times the preceding 20-session median, although five-session average volume was 1.3676 times that median. The maximum close-path drawdown within 63 sessions was -15.5060%. This combination supports a strong rebound/continuation interpretation but does not establish a confirmed breakout: price had not cleared the prior closing high, one latest-session volume ratio was not elevated, and the observed path could absorb large reversals.

The current empirical regime is defined by close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, and positive 21-session return. For 5 sessions, the regime-conditioned historical positive-return frequency was 55.4517% (178/321), median +0.4974%, 10th/90th percentiles -7.5762%/+6.7425%; the unconditional base rate was 58.6207% (374/638), median +1.1988%, 10th/90th -7.5914%/+9.7238%. For 21 sessions, conditional frequency was 63.8629% (205/321), median +2.8939%, 10th/90th -12.6204%/+15.5652%; unconditional was 68.3386% (436/638), median +4.7772%, 10th/90th -12.4354%/+19.9845%. For 63 sessions, conditional frequency was 65.7321% (211/321), median +10.6427%, 10th/90th -20.6472%/+36.7049%; unconditional was 75.3918% (481/638), median +13.4654%, 10th/90th -12.5658%/+41.4201%. These are historical empirical frequencies from one finite 2023-12-05 to 2026-06-23 lookback. Forward windows overlap and observations are dependent; the figures are not calibrated forecast probabilities, causal estimates or guarantees. A change in any regime sign would invalidate this conditional comparison and require recomputation.

For the 63-session mandate, the strongest continuation case is persistence above rising moving averages plus continued positive excess-return signs versus both SPY and XLK, followed by a completed close above the prior 21-session closing high with repeated—not single-session—volume support. The strongest opposing path is that the +26.5043% 63-session advance and near-high price represent an extended rebound: the slight 5-session lag to XLK, latest volume near its median, 55.0458% 63-session realized volatility and -15.5060% internal drawdown show that absolute strength can coexist with substantial path risk. Technical leadership is supported conditionally, but not low-volatility persistence.

The fixed external context is mixed and is not watchlist breadth: SPY returned +2.1112%, +1.0004% and +5.4254% over 5/21/63 sessions; IWM returned +0.7260%, -4.2506% and -2.7462%; HYG returned +0.3700%, -1.1808% and -1.5024%. This supplies broad-equity, small-cap and high-yield reference paths only; it does not establish news causality or explain ANET's move.

gaps.description: Stronger breakout conviction would require subsequent completed closes above the prior 21-session closing high with sustained volume, plus a recomputed out-of-sample or non-overlapping regime study. The supplied 638 historical starting points use overlapping forward windows from one finite history, so persistence and calibrated forecast probability are not established.

assumptions: All comparisons use the same 2026-09-22 completed-session cutoff, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price-return convention.
The $195.506 review level is the frozen SMA20 observed on 2026-09-22, not a future dynamic moving average and not an order level.
Relative-leadership conclusions are descriptive and conditional on recomputation from matched completed sessions; they are separate from valuation and fundamentals.
arguments.counter_thesis: The bullish level trend may be a late-stage rebound rather than durable leadership. ANET had already gained 26.5043% over 63 sessions, experienced a 15.5060% close-path drawdown within that window, sat just below the prior 21-session closing high, and slightly lagged XLK over the latest five sessions. A completed close below the frozen SMA20 checkpoint followed by negative 21-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK would shift the interpretation from volatile leadership to deteriorating momentum; loss of the 63-session excess-return signs would invalidate the longer-window leadership case as well.

review_conditions.description: Research checkpoint: a completed split-adjusted close below the frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level of $195.506 before expiry would weaken the positive price-level trend and increase the weight placed on the observed -15.5060% 63-session drawdown path. This is a frozen analytical threshold, not a future dynamic average or trade instruction.

Recompute matched 21- and 63-session ANET excess price returns versus both SPY and XLK after new completed sessions. If both 21-session signs turn negative, downgrade the medium-window leadership thesis to a fading rebound; if either 63-session sign also turns negative, invalidate longer-window leadership against that benchmark. Continued positive 21- and 63-session signs, especially after a completed close above the then-prior 21-session closing high on sustained multi-session volume, would strengthen continuation.
